title: Extraction and cleansing of data for a non-targeted analysis of high-resolution mass spectrometry data of wastewater
author: Verkh, Rozman, et al.

steps.title: Load raw LC‑HRMS data
steps.instruction: Import the Orbitrap Velos LC‑HRMS files (filtered wastewater samples and blanks, recorded in triplicate at 100 000 FWHM resolution) into the custom MZmine 2.26 workflow.

steps.title: Set MZmine processing parameters
steps.instruction: Configure MZmine 2.26 with the following options: mass tolerance = 5 ppm; signal‑to‑baseline threshold = 3 (ignore lower signals); peak duration = 0.05–8.00 min; atomic‑ratio limits for formula prediction H/C < 3.2, O/C < 1.2, N/C < 1.3, S/C < 0.8; isotopic grouping window = 60 ppm; allowed charges = ±1 or ±2; duplicate‑removal tolerances m/z = 3 ppm and retention time = 0.03 min; list of adducts to be excluded (see step 4).

steps.title: Correct m/z values with internal standards
steps.instruction: Run the provided R script that fits a linear model to internal‑standard (IS) m/z values (CSV files with the required column order) and applies the correction to all extracted signals within MZmine.

steps.title: Detect peaks and filter noise
steps.instruction: Execute peak detection in MZmine using the parameters set in step 2; ignore satellite signals assuming 1 × 10⁵ mass resolution; keep only monoisotopic features that have at least one consecutive isotopologue.

steps.title: Subtract solvent blank signal
steps.instruction: For each detected feature, subtract the intensity measured in the matching solvent blank from the sample intensity; do not apply any mathematical baseline correction.

steps.title: Group isotopes and remove ungrouped signals
steps.instruction: Group isotopic patterns using a 60 ppm window (default distance ≈1.0033 Da); discard any feature that cannot be grouped, ensuring only molecular features with an isotopic pattern remain.

steps.title: Remove adduct features
steps.instruction: Filter out features identified as the following adducts: in positive mode – [M+NH₄]⁺, [M+Na]⁺, [M+2Na]²⁺, [M+K]⁺, [M+2K]²⁺, [M+CH₃OH]⁺; in negative mode – [M−H₂O−H]⁻, [M−2(H₂O)−H]⁻, [M−2H+K]⁻, [M−2H+Na]⁻, [M+Cl]⁻, [M−H+HAc]⁻, [M+Br]⁻, [M−H+FA]⁻.

steps.title: Skip intensity normalization
steps.instruction: Do not perform any ion‑suppression correction or intensity normalization; retain the original spectra because normalization increased CV in replicates.

steps.title: Predict molecular formulae
steps.instruction: Run MZmine’s formula‑prediction module on features with neutral mass < 1000 Da, applying the atomic‑ratio limits from step 2 and selecting the candidate with the highest isotopic‑pattern score.

steps.title: Apply gap‑filling and CV filtering
steps.instruction: Use MZmine’s gap‑filling algorithm to recover missed peaks across samples; afterwards remove any feature whose coefficient of variation (CV) across triplicates exceeds 30 % and any signal with a sample‑to‑blank ratio < 3.

steps.title: Final noise reduction in R
steps.instruction: Run the supplied R function to delete any remaining entries with triplicate intensity CV > 30 % and to enforce the RatioSample:Blank ≥ 3 rule, producing the final cleaned feature table.
